To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tree amplitudes in scalar field theories are non-perturbantive at energies and multiplicities that are within the reach of present day experiments.

the cross section σ( q q→nH ) in the Standard Model (SM) becomes nonperturbative in the tree approximation at CM energy and multiplicity approximately given by √s 100–300TeV2/mH, nmH/ √s2 3, where mH and nmH are the mass and multiplicity of the Higgs boson.

the perturbative expansion breaks down in theories with scalons at energies √ s 10–30 TeV 2/mH, and that the overlap with the classical scalar field configuration becomes unsuppressed at these energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to define the perturbation expansion in a theory with scalars.
the question whether the tree approximation is valid in a theory with scalars, such as the standard model, when the scalar mass mH is not much smaller than the energy scale √ s.
the question of whether the Higgs field can be treated classically, as in the old phenomenological models, in the high energy regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tree amplitudes in the standard model become nonperturbative for Higgs masses in excess of about 300 GeV, and the same conclusion applies for the standard SUSY Higgs model with two doublet scalars.
perturbation theory is not applicable at tree level to processes involving the production of a large number of scalar bosons.
the perturbation series in the standard model is not convergent for tree amplitudes, and that it is not clear whether it is convergent for loop corrections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tree level perturbation theory in theories with scalar fields becomes nonperturbative at high energy and large multiplicity.
the standard model is non-perturbatively non-renormalizable at tree level, and that this is not a triviality problem.
tree level perturbative unitarity in theories with scalers is violated at a scale which is not necessarily the triviality scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tree amplitudes in scalar theories are not perturbative in λ, but rather in λ/√s.
tree-level amplitudes can be non-perturbatively large even when the coupling constant is weak, and the perturbation series in the coupling constant can still be asymptotic.
the perturbative expansion of the cross section in powers of λ breaks down in tree approximation at high energies.
